security_spec.violation_condition: If QEMU implements IOPMP MDCFG table write handling, and the emulation allows MDCFG(m).t values that create overlapping or inverted entry ranges (MDCFG(k).t > MDCFG(m).t for k < m) without enforcing the two mandatory constraints (at-most-one-MD ownership per entry, and lower-indexed MDs getting lower-indexed entries), then guest software relying on MDCFG entry partitioning to isolate I/O domains could have enforcement silently broken. The PR's removal of reference-behavior guidance (previously a NOTE listing options like 'correct the values', 'reject the write', or 'leave the improper setting') removes safe defaults that a QEMU developer might otherwise follow, placing full burden on the implementer to pick a secure implementation-dependent behavior.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: MDCFG write handler that stores t fields without validating monotonicity or without enforcing at-most-one-MD ownership post-write; lookup logic that double-assigns entries when MDCFG ranges overlap; missing W1C/WARL semantics on MDCFG registers allowing guest to craft improper settings
security_spec.summary: QEMU IOPMP MDCFG implementation must self-enforce the two improper-setting constraints (at-most-one-MD per entry, lower-index-MD → lower-index-entries) since the spec makes behavior implementation-dependent and dropped the safe-reference NOTE; failure to validate MDCFG monotonicity on write would allow a malicious guest to overlap memory domains, granting an I/O device access to regions outside its intended MD

findings.finding: QEMU does not implement IOPMP or MDCFG tables. A comprehensive search of the entire QEMU source tree found zero references to 'iopmp', 'IOPMP', 'mdcfg', or 'MDCFG' in any file. The RISC-V IOMMU (hw/riscv/riscv-iommu.c) implements I/O address translation but is architecturally separate from IOPMP, which is an I/O bus master access control mechanism. The CPU-side PMP (target/riscv/pmp.c) controls only hart-initiated memory accesses. The IOPMP specification exists at /home/yzs/riscv/rv-isa-sec/spec_ref/riscv-iopmp/ with a complete reference model, but no corresponding QEMU emulation code exists. The PR titled 'Clarify MDCFG Table' appears to be a spec-only change removing reference-behavior guidance (the NOTE listing options like 'correct the values', 'reject the write', or 'leave the improper setting') from the IOPMP specification document itself, not a QEMU code change.
findings.snippet: No IOPMP/MDCFG code found in QEMU source tree.

spec_citations.excerpt: The MDCFG Table is used to map a memory domain to its own entries... An entry can belong to at most one memory domain... When the MDCFG Table has an improper setting... the following conditions must be held: an entry must belong to at most one memory domain; and the index of an entry in a lower-indexed memory domain must be lower than that in a higher-indexed memory domain.
Field 't' is WARL... If MDCFG(m-1).t > MDCFG(m).t, then MDCFG Table is improperly programmed. Please refer to MDCFG Table for IOPMP behavior of improperly programming.

Here is a non-exhaustive list of behaviors for handling improper settings on MDCFG Table: correct the values, reject write accesses that produce improper settings, or leave the improper setting but entry association becomes undefined for affected MDs.
